US-003.recommendation: No grace period. Delete straight away, but make the student type DELETE to confirm.
US-003.why: A typed confirmation stops accidental deletions without the extra work of scheduled deletion jobs.
add_criteria: The "Delete account" button stays disabled until the student types DELETE in the confirmation box.
US-003.resolution: No grace period; the account is deleted immediately after the student types DELETE to confirm.

US-005.recommendation: No archiving in this version. Deleting a subject is enough for a one-semester project; archiving goes to Future Scope.
US-005.why: Archiving touches every list and report, which is a lot of work for little benefit within one semester.
US-005.resolution: Archiving subjects is out of scope for this version and listed under Future Scope.

US-006.recommendation: One exam date per subject. A subject with a separate practical exam is added as its own subject, for example "DBMS Practical".
US-006.why: This keeps the data model as it is while still covering theory and practical exams.
US-006.resolution: One exam date per subject; separate practical or theory exams are added as separate subjects.

US-007.recommendation: Don't model holidays. Attendance warnings use only classes the student has logged; the timetable only shows today's classes and the next class date.
US-007.why: Predicting future classes needs a holiday calendar the app doesn't have. Using logged classes keeps warnings correct.
add_criteria: Attendance percentages and warnings use only logged attendance records, never classes predicted from the timetable.
US-007.resolution: Holidays aren't modelled; warnings use logged attendance only, and the timetable is used for today's classes and the next class date.

US-010.recommendation: Use a 1.5× rule: each weak subject gets at least 1.5 times the total minutes of every non-weak subject with the same or a later exam date.
US-010.why: A number makes the rule testable, and the planner can reject an AI plan that breaks it.
add_criteria: Each weak subject's total planned minutes are at least 1.5 times those of every non-weak subject whose exam date is the same or later.
US-010.resolution: Weak subjects get at least 1.5 times the minutes of non-weak subjects with the same or a later exam date.

US-011.recommendation: One value for every day in this version. Separate weekday and weekend hours go to Future Scope.
US-011.why: A single number keeps the planner form and the AI prompt simple.
US-011.resolution: One daily study-hours value applies to every day; per-weekday hours are Future Scope.

US-013.recommendation: Don't change the status automatically. A planned session from a past date shows "Not marked", and the dashboard asks the student to mark it completed or missed.
US-013.why: Automatic changes would trigger re-plans the student didn't ask for and use AI requests.
add_criteria: A planned session dated before today shows a "Not marked" label, and the dashboard lists it with buttons to mark it completed or missed.
US-013.resolution: Past planned sessions aren't changed automatically; they show "Not marked" and the dashboard prompts the student.

US-017.recommendation: Keep the 10 MB limit and accept only PDF and plain text. Word and PowerPoint go to Future Scope; students can save those files as PDF.
US-017.why: PDF text extraction is reliable and free; each extra format needs another library and more testing.
US-017.resolution: 10 MB limit; PDF and plain text only. Word and PowerPoint support is Future Scope.

US-018.why: A fixed size keeps AI requests small, makes scores comparable between attempts, and is easy to test.
replace_criteria: Each successfully processed note has a quiz of 5 to 10 multiple-choice questions.
Each successfully processed note has a quiz of exactly 8 multiple-choice questions.

US-019.recommendation: No XP for quizzes in this version.
US-019.why: Quizzes can be retaken any number of times, so quiz XP would be easy to farm. XP stays tied to assignments and study sessions.
US-019.resolution: Quizzes don't award XP in this version.

US-024.recommendation: Add an optional description of up to 500 characters. Keep due dates as dates only, since course deadlines are given as dates.
US-024.why: A description holds instructions copied from the group chat; a due time adds time-zone complexity for little gain.
add_criteria: The student can add an optional description of up to 500 characters; longer text is rejected with a message.
US-024.resolution: Assignments get an optional description (needs a description column on Assignment); due dates stay date-only.

US-027.recommendation: Yes. Without due times, "due today or tomorrow" is the clearest rule.
US-027.why: It matches how students read deadlines and needs no extra data.
US-027.resolution: "Due soon" means due today or tomorrow in the student's time zone.

US-029.recommendation: In-app reminders only for this version, as ADR-019 proposes. Email reminders go to Future Scope.
US-029.why: Free hosting can't run a reliable scheduler for emails.
US-029.resolution: Reminders are in-app only; email reminders are Future Scope.

US-033.recommendation: Yes. Update TC-05 in the synopsis to expect an "At risk" warning at 18 of 24.
US-033.why: Warning before a shortfall is this feature's main promise, and at 18 of 24 one more absence drops the student to 72%.
US-033.resolution: TC-05 in the synopsis is updated to expect an "At risk" warning at 18 of 24.

US-034.recommendation: Keep 20 XP per assignment and 10 XP per study session, with no XP for quizzes (see US-019).
US-034.why: Assignments take more effort than one session, and the round numbers are easy to explain.
US-034.resolution: 20 XP per completed assignment, 10 XP per completed study session, none for quizzes.

US-035.recommendation: No. Only completing an assignment or a study session counts as activity.
US-035.why: The streak should measure studying, not record-keeping.
US-035.resolution: Only completing an assignment or a study session counts towards the streak.

US-036.recommendation: Four badges: First Step, 7-Day Streak, Assignment Ace and Perfect Score.
US-036.why: Four badges cover a first win, consistency, workload and mastery without much extra code.
replace_criteria: The full badge list and the conditions for each are defined before this story is built.

The badges are: First Step (first completed assignment or study session), 7-Day Streak (streak reaches 7), Assignment Ace (10 assignments completed) and Perfect Score (every question right on a quiz).
US-036.resolution: Badges: First Step, 7-Day Streak, Assignment Ace and Perfect Score.

US-037.recommendation: Yes, a flat 100 XP per level.
US-037.why: It's easy to explain to students and to test.

US-039.recommendation: Yes. Remove focus time from §5.5 of the synopsis.
US-039.why: Nothing in the app records focus time, so the report can't show it.
US-039.resolution: Focus time is removed from the report and from synopsis §5.5.
